meta.title: Thomas Scientific: the growth plan
meta.subject: Thomas Scientific (Swedesboro NJ; BSP portfolio company since Jan 2022)
meta.thesis: From distributor to lab-supply-chain company: target-account selling into 27.5k scored lab and hospital sites, punchout ordering, VMI, private label and specialty verticals; regional add-ons; AI agents for quoting, forecasting and account health.
meta.method: Expansion-phase data points are computed from repo datasets: data/ts_sites.json (27,503 sites, aggregated by region only: counts by vertical, priority label and archetype, and summed 2023 CMS allowed amounts), data/ts_parents.json (top 500 parents), data/research/ma_targets_fl_ts.json (25 Thomas Scientific targets, ZoomInfo revenue estimates), Thomas Scientific filings (capital structure and estimates), public comparables (lab-distribution medians), PE landscape (Calibre, Sterling), BSP firm profile (Smith + Howard timeline and Thomas add-ons) and ServiceOS evidence (LabOS KPI benchmarks kb-ts-1..3, ve-06, ra-ts). External evidence was gathered on 2026-10-06 by web search and direct fetches of SEC filings (Avantor FY2025 10-K, VWR FY2014 10-K), state/federal pages (NJDOL), banker reports (Houlihan Lokey) and vendor case studies. Growth-lever and KPI targets are benchmarks or labelled assumptions; the KPI roadmap is an analyst assumption anchored to the Thomas Scientific filings estimate table.
caveats: Thomas Scientific is a stressed credit: first-lien loan at 88.3% of par (Jun-2026), maturity 2027-12-14, common equity marked near zero, est. leverage 7-10x. Every lever is sequenced behind liquidity and refinancing.
Company revenue, EBITDA and headcount are low-confidence analyst estimates (Thomas Scientific filings), not company disclosures; the KPI roadmap inherits that uncertainty.

data/research/market_evidence.json and a KPI targets dataset were not present in the repo at build time; KPI targets use ServiceOS evidence KPI benchmark items (kb-ts-*) and external sources, labelled as assumptions.

Thomas lab-site list scores are from a legacy targeting tool (NPPES, CMS 2023, CLIA, Hospital Compare); site counts are aggregated by region only, and the CMS allowed amount is Medicare billing, not lab-supply spend.
Vendor case studies (InstaLILY, Conexiom, Algolia, Conga/PROS, HighRadius, Flagship VMI) are self-reported and unaudited; treat them as upper bounds. weeks to deploy values are analyst estimates.
Market-size figures for cleanroom, cannabis testing and healthcare cold chain come from market-research firms whose forecasts vary widely.
The McKinsey forecasting figures and the Antylia/GTCR details come from search-engine extracts because the primary pages blocked automated fetches.
ZoomInfo revenue estimates for add-on targets are modeled and can be far off.
narrative: Thomas is Fund I's largest and most stressed position: lenders mark the first-lien loan at 88% of par, the common near zero, and the loan matures in December 2027.
This plan puts cash and refinancing first and growth second; the growth story is what earns the refinancing.

Smith + Howard shows the shape: a regional leader that grew from about 100 to 800 people, 1 to 11 locations and nearly 4x revenue through nine add-ons, specialist capabilities and technology investment.
For Thomas the equivalent is not 4x revenue; it is turning a 125-year-old distributor into a lab supply-chain portfolio company that buyers value above a commodity distributor.
The demand map already exists: 27,503 scored lab, pathology and hospital sites, 713 rated Pursue and 2,317 Nurture, and the top 500 parent organizations account for 832 of the scored sites.
An inside-sales academy on Grainger's model, with 4 weeks of training and then a 100-account book, would need about 30 books to cover every Pursue and Nurture site.
Digital is table stakes: Avantor does about 80% of transactions online, and Grainger's ePro channels are about 40% of connected orders, growing far faster than rep-led sales.
Margin has to come from mix: private label was 19% of VWR's sales at higher margins, AI pricing tools have added about 120 basis points at large distributors, and VMI makes accounts sticky.
Cleanroom, cannabis-testing, cold-chain and forensics programs add faster-growing niches on top of a lab-distribution market growing about 1.5% a year.
AI agents for quoting, order entry, search, forecasting, collections and account health are cheap relative to the cash they release; each day of DSO is worth about $0.8M.
Add-ons restart only when funded: one $15-25M regional or specialty distributor a year (Midland, MIDSCI, Capitol, Valutek, Genesee), competing mainly against Calibre Scientific.
On our assumptions EBITDA moves from about $30M to about $42.5M in 36 months, which brings leverage back near 6x and inside today's unitranche market, the bar for an amend-and-extend, recap or sale.

items.move: Entry: buy a respected regional leader, then fund the build
items.what_happened: BSP made a strategic anchor investment in Smith + Howard, then a single-office Atlanta CPA firm of about 100 professionals.
items.ts_translation: Thomas is already the anchor company (founded 1900, 9 distribution centers). The analogous step is to re-underwrite it as a growth company: name the 27.5k-site target universe, fund the commercial engine, and stop treating it as a stand-alone distributor.

items.move: First geographic hop by merger with a like-minded regional firm
items.what_happened: Smith + Howard joined forces with Market Street Partners (Chattanooga), its first move outside Atlanta.
items.ts_translation: Thomas already did this with NCI (Minneapolis, 2022) and Arrowhead (Lenexa KS, 2023). The next hop should follow target-account density: Texas, Oklahoma, Louisiana and Arkansas (5,766 scored sites) and the West (5,786) have no Thomas stocking point except the Carlyle-era E&K (Santa Clara) and American Cleanstat (Irvine).

items.move: Buy a specialist capability, not just revenue
items.what_happened: Smith + Howard acquired JMM CPAs (Chicago) to expand its benefit-plan audit practice, a specialty service line it could sell across the whole client base.
items.ts_translation: For Thomas the specialist buys are cleanroom/controlled-environment consumables (Valutek, Micronova), reagents and buffers (RICCA, Boston BioProducts) and private-label lab essentials (MIDSCI PR1MA, Genesee): each adds a margin-accretive line that sells into all nine DCs.

items.move: Add an adjacent service that deepens client relationships
items.what_happened: Smith + Howard acquired VIP Search / VIP Solutions (Dallas), adding recruiting and outsourced accounting services next to audit and tax.
items.ts_translation: Thomas analog: onsite services (VMI, stockroom management, equipment tracking). Avantor runs ~2,000 service associates side by side with customers; that service layer is what makes a distributor sticky.

items.move: Densify one region with a cadence of tuck-ins
items.what_happened: Fahrenheit Advisors (Richmond), Smith Kesler (Carolinas), Horton Lee & Burnett (Birmingham) and Bauknight Pietras & Stormer (South Carolina) built a Southeast cluster, roughly one deal every four months.
items.ts_translation: Thomas has made no acquisition since Oct 2023. Restart a disciplined cadence of one $5-25M tuck-in every 4-6 months once liquidity allows; regional distributors trade near 0.8x sales (Denville precedent), well below company value.

items.move: Invest in technology, AI and an offshore delivery center
items.what_happened: Geels Norton (cyber/SOC) joined Smith + Howard; the CEO credits investments in leadership, technology, AI-enabled capabilities and an offshore delivery center in India for the transformation.
items.ts_translation: Thomas analog: AI agents for quoting, order entry, search and collections (see AI-agent items) and a shared-service back office, aimed at lowering cost-to-serve on ~$700 average orders.

items.move: Exit to an upmarket growth buyer at national scale
items.what_happened: BSP sold Smith + Howard to TPG Growth after about 3.7 years: ~100 -> ~800 professionals, 1 -> 11 locations (Southeast US + India), 9 acquisitions, nearly 4x revenue.
items.ts_translation: The Thomas version of "national scale" is not 4x revenue; it is a re-rated, refinanced portfolio company with clean cash interest coverage and a visible digital/private-label margin story before the Dec-2027 loan maturity.

items.move: Carve-out lab-products distributor rebuilt through 15 add-ons and a portfolio sale
items.what_happened: GTCR bought Cole-Parmer in a 2014 carve-out from Thermo Fisher, made 15 add-on acquisitions, sold the Masterflex bioprocessing unit to Avantor for $2.9B (2021), and sold the remaining Antylia Scientific to Brookfield and CDPQ for ~$1.34B (2025).
items.ts_translation: Closest same-vertical precedent: value came from proprietary/manufactured lines and selective divestiture, not from distribution volume alone. Thomas should identify which lines (cleanroom, forensics, private label) could be valued separately.
items.note: Figures from search-engine extract of the deal note and corroborating trackers (PrivSource, AlternativesWatch $1.34B); GTCR release itself not fetched.

items.move: Buy-and-build of lab distributors plus proprietary manufacturing and service
items.what_happened: StoneCalibre launched Calibre Scientific on Jan 1 2018 and lists ~40+ acquisitions through Oct 2024 (PE landscape counts 64+), organized into Calibre Scientific (proprietary products), Calibre Lab (distribution) and Calibre Tec (service).
items.ts_translation: Calibre is the most active bidder for the same U.S. chromatography, consumables and glassware add-ons. Its three-division model (own brand + distribution + service) is the shape Thomas should copy, and its European focus leaves U.S. regional distributors open.

items.name: Stabilize the core and buy time
items.geography: Northeast / Mid-Atlantic core (NJ, PA, NY, DE, MD, MA, CT, RI, NH, VT, ME) served from Swedesboro NJ and the Massachusetts cleanroom hubs (Denville/Holliston, Quintana/Haverhill, Day/Dracut)
items.thesis: Thomas is a stressed credit (est. EBITDA $25-35M, leverage 7-10x, first-lien loan marked at 88.3% of par, maturity 2027-12-14). The first six months are about cash: price discipline, working capital, and a named-account program in the home region, so the lender conversation in 2027 is about growth rather than survival.

items.lever: Named-account coverage of scored diagnostics labs and health systems
items.unit: sites under named rep or digital coverage (Pursue + Nurture)
items.evidence: Thomas lab-site list scores 27,503 lab/hospital/pathology sites: 713 Pursue, 2,317 Nurture. The top 500 parent organizations own 832 sites. Thomas's current coverage of these sites is not known (baseline null). Avantor fields ~3,400 sales staff incl. 170+ specialists against 300,000+ customer locations.

Avantor FY2025 10-K: "approximately 80% of our transactions came from our digital channels". VWR's FY2014 10-K said over half of orders came from e-commerce, so the leader moved from ~50% to ~80% in a decade. Thomas digital share is undisclosed.

items.lever: Punchout / eProcurement penetration of contract accounts
items.evidence: Grainger (Q4 2025): ePro is "closer to 40%" of connected ordering, and most contract customers use both ePro and KeepStock, making relationships "stickier". Digital Endless Assortment grew ~15.6% vs ~2.1% for rep-led High-Touch in 2025.

items.lever: Vendor-managed inventory (VMI) and onsite stockroom services
items.unit: % reduction in customer lab inventory (value delivered to customer)
items.evidence: A bioscience VMI program on the 225 most-used consumables cut inventory 34%, excess work 44% and returned 52 hrs/month to scientists. Avantor runs ~2,000 onsite service associates handling procurement, stockroom and equipment tracking; Fisher Scientific runs Unity Lab Services VMI.

items.unit: % of net sales from private label
items.evidence: VWR FY2014 10-K: private label ~19% of net sales and "generally provide us higher margins". Denville (Thomas's 2018 private-label-heavy add-on) ran ~34.8% gross margin. Avantor FY2025: proprietary materials & consumables $3.45B vs third-party $3.10B.

Conga (formerly PROS) case: a Fortune 500 distributor ($7.2B revenue, ~2M SKUs) gained 120 bps of margin since Apr 2021 when a 50 bp decline had been projected; sales override rates fell from 60-70%. On Thomas's est. $285M revenue, 50-120 bps is ~$1.4-3.4M EBITDA.

Technavio forecasts cleanroom consumables growing by $7.18B at a 7.3% CAGR 2024-2029, versus a 1.5% median latest-year growth for listed lab distributors (public comparables). Thomas already owns NCI, Quintana, Day and American Cleanstat in this niche; Valutek ($100M ZoomInfo est.) and Micronova are scored targets.

IMARC: U.S. cannabis testing market $391.1M (2024) to $942.9M by 2033 (10.3% CAGR). Thomas already sells into the segment (listed as a trade creditor in the 2026 Cannabist Co. bankruptcy), so credit screening must come with the push.
items.note: Market-research estimate; credit risk in cannabis operators is high.

items.unit: % CAGR, healthcare logistics (cold chain fastest-growing segment)
items.evidence: Healthcare logistics valued at $96.15B in 2025, growing 9.07% a year, with cold chain the fastest-growing segment as biologics, mRNA and cell therapies scale. Thomas would sell validated shippers, dry ice, ULT storage and monitoring into the same diagnostics and biopharma accounts.

items.lever: Federal and forensics channel (DLA ECAT, NIH/CDC BPAs, ATF)
items.unit: USD federal obligations per fiscal year (target is an assumption)
items.evidence: USASpending: Thomas federal obligations were $8.30M in FY2025 (vs $84-91M in COVID years); vehicles include DLA ECAT, NIH and CDC BPAs and a 2026 ATF forensic-imaging BPA that came with Arrowhead Forensics.

items.job_to_be_done: Read inbound RFQ emails and web forms, match line items to the catalog, pull contract pricing and return a quote within the hour; escalate the hard ones to inside sales.
items.who_it_helps: Inside sales reps and customer service
items.metric_claim: A national industrial-automation distributor's agents answered 6,000+ emails and returned ~1,500 quotes in the first month, unlocking 10,000+ hours a year; win probability falls sharply after the first hour.
items.note: Vendor case study; weeks to deploy is an estimate.

items.job_to_be_done: Turn emailed/PDF purchase orders into ERP sales orders without keying.
items.who_it_helps: Customer service reps; customers waiting on confirmations
items.metric_claim: ADI Global eliminated manual processing of 1,700 orders/day and saved 142 hours/day for 600+ inside sales reps.
items.cost_model: Annual subscription priced on document/order volume (quote-based)

items.job_to_be_done: Typo-tolerant search over CAS numbers, part numbers and specs; suggest in-stock or private-label equivalents.
items.who_it_helps: Scientists and buyers ordering online; reps answering "do you have an equivalent?"
items.metric_claim: Swedol (B2B distributor) saw a 22% higher conversion rate, 26% more time on site and 7.5% more searches after moving to Algolia.
items.cost_model: Usage-based: Algolia Grow plan 10,000 searches/month free, then $0.50 per 1,000 requests

items.job_to_be_done: Forecast SKU x DC demand, set reorder points, flag excess and slow stock across nine DCs and VMI sites.
items.metric_claim: McKinsey: AI-driven forecasting can cut forecast error 20-50% and lost sales from stockouts by up to 65%.
items.cost_model: Netstock from about $400-900/month (third-party listing); enterprise suites quote-based
items.note: McKinsey page blocked automated fetch; figures from search-engine extracts of the article. Netstock pricing from ServiceOS evidence vs-ts-3.

items.job_to_be_done: Score every account for churn risk and wallet-share gap; tell reps whom to call and what to pitch.
items.who_it_helps: Account managers and inside sales; sales leadership
items.metric_claim: Proton.ai computes a score from churn likelihood and wallet-share opportunity and recommends next-best products and contacts for distributor reps.
items.note: Proton's published uplift figures (e.g., 8% revenue per rep) could not be fetched from a primary page; metric value left null.

items.job_to_be_done: Recommend deal prices by customer, SKU and cost change; stop below-floor quotes.
items.metric_claim: A Fortune 500 distributor gained 120 bps of margin with AI pricing guidance covering 75% of business.

items.job_to_be_done: Prioritize past-due accounts, send dunning, match remittances to invoices.
items.who_it_helps: AR/credit team; treasury (liquidity before the 2027 maturity)
items.metric_claim: Industrial distributor DXP cut DSO by 20 days, raised collector productivity 40% and added $20M of cash flow across 15,000+ customers.
items.note: Vendor case study. On ~$285M revenue, each day of DSO is ~$0.8M of cash.

items.job_to_be_done: Surface account insights, new contacts and coaching moments for each rep.
items.metric_claim: Grainger's SellerInsights uses AI to deliver actionable insights, identify new customer contacts and strengthen coaching; digital channels grew ~15.6% vs ~2.1% rep-led in 2025.

items.job_to_be_done: Answer product, availability and order-status questions on the website and in punchout, 24/7.
items.who_it_helps: Buyers who prefer not to call a rep; customer service
items.metric_claim: Gartner (Aug-Sep 2025, n=646): 67% of B2B buyers prefer a rep-free buying experience and 45% used AI during a recent purchase.

items.evidence: Grainger runs a 4-week paid Inside Sales Academy; graduates receive a book of 100+ mid-size accounts in 1-2 industries. For Thomas, 713 Pursue + 2,317 Nurture sites is ~30 books of 100.

items.evidence: Distribution Strategy (Mike Kunkle): structured onboarding cut ramp time 23-52% across four companies and lifted sales per rep 48% in the 90 days after onboarding.

items.evidence: Avantor's ~2,000 service associates work side by side with customers on procurement, logistics, inventory and stockroom management, chemical and equipment tracking.

items.facts: Closed 2021-12-14 at L+625 (1% floor), maturity 2027-12-14. MFIC Jun-2026: term loan par $32.85M marked at 88.3% of par; revolver $2.35M drawn, $0.74M undrawn; total facility est. $180-300M.
items.implication: The maturity is 14 months away and the loan trades as distressed. Any growth plan must first secure an amend-and-extend or refinancing.

items.instrument: Coupon history: PIK amendment and return to cash pay
items.facts: Q4-2024 amendment converted part of the coupon to PIK (SOFR+340 cash + 4.50% PIK); principal accreted ~4.4% in 2025; Q1-2026 the loan returned to all-cash SOFR+640.
items.implication: Cash interest coverage is est. ~1.0-1.3x. Working-capital release (DSO, inventory) is the fastest internal source of cash.

items.instrument: Sponsor equity: BSP-TS, LP and preferred top-ups
items.facts: BSP-TS, LP raised $236.1M at close (Dec 2021), $257.1M cumulative by Jan 2024 (+$21.0M), with preferred units ranking above common; common equity is marked near zero (Barings co-invest stake $6.9K on ~$5M).
items.implication: New money is likely to come as preferred or structured equity. Add-ons in the next 12 months must be small, cash-light (earn-outs, seller notes, rollover equity) or funded with new capital.

items.instrument: Sector leverage norms for a refinancing
items.facts: Houlihan Lokey (Oct 2025) new-issue private credit for $20-100M EBITDA borrowers: unitranche 5.25x-6.25x at S+450-525, first lien 3.75x-4.75x; median net total leverage ~4.7x (Sep-2025).
items.implication: At est. $25-35M EBITDA a market unitranche supports ~$130-220M of debt against est. $210-310M outstanding. Closing that gap needs EBITDA growth to ~$40-45M, equity paydown, or a lender-led solution.

items.facts: Denville Scientific (2018) was bought for ~$20M on ~$25M revenue (~0.8x sales, ~35% gross margin). GF Data: average LMM purchase multiple 7.2x TTM adjusted EBITDA in 2025.
items.implication: Small regional distributors bought at 5-7x and folded into a company valued higher add value through multiple arbitrage, but only once the company can fund them.
